-ire verbs: Infinitive verbs ending in -ire fall into the third conjugation class. Examples include "dormire" (to sleep), "partire" (to leave), and "capire" (to understand).

Infinitive verbs are important because they serve as the dictionary form of the verb and do not change based on the subject or tense. info:
The Italian infinitive verb form is the base or unconjugated form of a verb. In Italian, infinitive verbs end in either -are, -ere, or -ire. These endings correspond to the three conjugation classes of verbs in the Italian language.

-are verbs: These verbs end in -are in their infinitive form. For example, "parlare" (to speak), "mangiare" (to eat), and "camminare" (to walk).

-ere verbs: Infinitive verbs ending in -ere belong to the second conjugation class. Examples include "leggere" (to read), "scrivere" (to write), and "vedere" (to see).

-ire verbs: Infinitive verbs ending in -ire fall into the third conjugation class. Examples include "dormire" (to sleep), "partire" (to leave), and "capire" (to understand).

Infinitive verbs are important because they serve as the dictionary form of the verb and do not change based on the subject or tense. To use a verb in a sentence, it needs to be conjugated to match the subject and the tense of the sentence. Conjugation involves changing the verb form based on the grammatical person (first person, second person, third person) and number (singular or plural) as well as the tense (past, present, future).
